NGA.note: Nothing on AI harm rules or an authority.
Nothing on AI used in government administration.
Nothing on AI in a sector's public system.

facts.fact: NITDA's interventions supported the development of N-ATLAS, an openly released AI language model with eight billion parameters and four speech recognition models in Nigerian languages, as presented by Raymond Onuoha of Lagos Business School.

N-ATLAS has attracted more than 140 registered collaborators and 18 third-party applications have been certified for integration with it, according to Onuoha; commercialisation and adoption are at an early stage.

NGA.note: Training described is for Nigerians generally, none for civil servants.
Data centres are mentioned only as infrastructure needed; no facility stated.
A call for inclusion in underserved communities only; no rural programme or survey figures.

facts.fact: NITDA reports it has trained and certified approximately 2.8 million Nigerians in digital skills under its SRAP 2.0 strategy, per Raymond Onuoha of Lagos Business School; no locations are stated.

NGA.note: SRAP 2.0 is an agency's own plan, noted and not assessed.
No nationally owned data centre stated.
Startup support and money mobilised are stated without a startup act, strategy or public fund under one.
Nothing on hubs, incubators or parks.
